fleetpulse.name: FleetPulse
fleetpulse.customDescription: Scalable, highly available SaaS of Go microservices (gRPC + REST) for fleet telemetry, device claiming, and firmware compliance.
fleetpulse.architecture: Go / gRPC / Kubernetes / PostgreSQL / NATS / AWS / Helm
fleetpulse.problem: Fleet operators struggled with managing heterogeneous IoT hardware, firmware compliance drift, and handling high-volume telemetry ingestion under burst traffic.
fleetpulse.approach: Architected Go microservices using gRPC and REST with multi-tenant JWT RBAC. Implemented core DSA paths: consistent hashing for device sharding, min-heap job scheduler, token-bucket rate limiter, LRU cache, and EWMA/z-score anomaly detection with leader election and dead-letter queues. Provisioned on Kubernetes with Helm and HPA, monitored with Prometheus/Grafana, and automated via GitHub Actions with an 80%+ coverage gate.
fleetpulse.result: Engineered idempotent retries and DLQs that handle burst telemetry, validated resilience with k6 load testing, and established automated canary and rolling updates.

payment-platform-java.name: ApexPay
payment-platform-java.customDescription: Enterprise payment platform with 6 Spring Boot microservices, choreographed Saga over 4 Kafka topics, and Transactional Outbox pattern.
payment-platform-java.architecture: Java 21 / Spring Boot 3 / Kafka / PostgreSQL / MongoDB / Kubernetes
payment-platform-java.problem: High-volume distributed transactions faced data inconsistency, partial failure during payment processing, and security compliance risks.
payment-platform-java.approach: Built 6 Spring Boot microservices across an 8-module Maven architecture using choreographed Sagas across 4 Kafka topics, Transactional Outbox pattern, idempotency keys, and dead-letter topics. Implemented Spring Security with BCrypt(12), 15-minute rotating JWTs, RBAC, account lockout, and rate limiting. Verified with TDD using JUnit 5, Mockito, and Testcontainers.
payment-platform-java.result: Achieved zero distributed state divergence across payment workflows. Enforced automated 6-stage GitLab CI/CD with SonarQube quality gates, Trivy container security scans, and OpenShift Kubernetes deployment monitored via 3 Grafana dashboards and ELK.

lendstrangler.name: LendStrangler
lendstrangler.customDescription: Incremental decomposition of a legacy lending monolith into 3 microservices using the Strangler Fig pattern with shadow verification.
lendstrangler.architecture: TypeScript / Node.js / RabbitMQ / React / Docker / ADRs
lendstrangler.problem: A legacy monolith lending system suffered from slow release cycles, high underwriting latency (85ms), and tight coupling between credit evaluation and loan servicing.
lendstrangler.approach: Decomposed the system into 3 independent microservices via the Strangler Fig pattern. Ran in shadow mode to verify identical output against production traffic before canary routing from 5% to 100%. Implemented a 5-event Saga with compensating transactions over RabbitMQ, Transactional Outbox, and idempotent consumers, documented comprehensively across 6 Architectural Decision Records (ADRs).
lendstrangler.result: Achieved 0.00% response diff during shadow mode, zero planned downtime during rollout, and slashed underwriting latency by 77% (from 85ms down to 19ms) backed by an 80%+ CI/CD coverage gate.
